A failed or timed-out lookup (exit 124 included) or an unreadable file (not a missing one: missing = no marker) makes that project `gitok: false` for the run: no note work, no release for it. The laptop logs one line `  [<dir>] không đọc được .git/info/exclude (<reason>), bỏ qua ghi chú của dự án này lần này` (`<dir>` = the laptop project folder path, `<reason>` = the exception text; screen in a manual run, phien.log in a quick or auto run, exit code unchanged); the box logs nothing. The scan result of the laptop also carries `excl`, the resolved path.
- Legacy. Records `exclude:<laptop|box>:<project>/<file>` = 1 written by 1.3.2 / 1.3.3 keep their meaning for the bare `/<name>` lines of that time until released. The planner releases a name when it is tracked on the other side (index or origin default), this side has an untracked copy, and (`fx` or such a record); the release object carries `legacy = true` exactly when the record exists. The pair is removed; a bare `/<name>` line is removed only with `legacy`; with `legacy` off and only a bare line present nothing is touched and the answer is "gone for sure". `unexclude` entries in the first put batch are `{project, name, legacy}`. Shared exclude files (1.3.6). Linked work trees of one repository share one `.git/info/exclude`, so a pair hides `/<name>` at the root of every one of them and belongs to every project on that file. A release keeps the line (box answer `kept`, laptop `Test-PhienSharedNote`) when another project sharing the file — box: any `config.json` project (`shared_projects`, A12); laptop: any `syncRepos` folder (the raw list, so duplicate folder names count), identified by `git rev-parse --git-common-dir --show-toplevel --show-prefix` (git resolves junction aliases) — holds a regular file `<name>` at its root that is tracked nowhere for it (neither index nor origin default), whose own release of that name is not in this run, and that git hides through a `/<name>` line of `info/exclude` (`git check-ignore -v -z --stdin`, NUL-separated fields, so no path is quoted; a `.gitignore` or global match is independent and does not keep the line). Holder candidates (one rule, both sides): a project is asked about only when it holds a regular, non-link file `<name>` at its root (a candidate); a project without one is never a holder, and no git failure about it fails the release. The laptop tests the file before its first git call; the box reads the one `rev-parse` it runs for every config project for Rule H by the same rule (`holds_note`): a failure other than "not a git repository" is an error for a candidate and a skip for any other project, as in 1.3.5 (git giving no answer at all for any config project still makes Rule H wait, "Git stays clean" in A12). A git failure is an error, not `kept`; `kept` means only a real holder. A git failure is any failure while asking about a candidate: no answer in time or git not started (on the box also in the upstream half of the holder check), a corrupt index, a `rev-parse` failure other than "not a git repository" (for example "detected dubious ownership"), or a `check-ignore` answer that is not four NUL-separated fields. The line then stays, the release gives the error line of "Release answers" with exit 1, the record is kept and the release is retried at every run (box: `shared_projects` or `pair_holders` returns None and `unexclude` False; laptop: `Test-PhienSharedNote` returns `'unknown'`). Only a candidate that git itself reports as "not a git repository" is skipped; both sides run git with `LC_ALL=C` so that this text can be matched (box `git()` passes it to the child; laptop `Invoke-GitQuiet` sets `$env:LC_ALL` around the child, which inherits the process environment — `ProcessStartInfo.EnvironmentVariables` is never used, its getter fails on Windows PowerShell 5.1 when two names differ only in case), and paths stay UTF-8. Two projects released in the same run do not hold the line for each other. A kept release prints, instead of the `ghi chú <file> giờ do git theo dõi …` line (which says the old copy can be deleted), `  [<project>] ghi chú <file>: dự án khác cùng kho trên <box|laptop> còn dùng dòng giấu /<file>, fcode chưa gỡ`, forgets nothing, keeps the exit code, is asked again at every run, and is not listed in `notes.released` (so the menu never says `xóa được` for it). It ends by a state change, but only while this project's old copy stays (a release is planned only then): the other copy becomes tracked, is deleted or shown (the next run removes the line), or both are released in one run. If the old copy of this project is deleted, or a `git pull` overwrites and tracks it, no release is planned any more and fcode never removes the pair: the user deletes the two lines `# fcode` and `/<name>` of `info/exclude` by hand. The old copy stays ignored meanwhile (a `git pull` there overwrites it silently); accepted over exposing the other project's untracked note. A user's own bare `/<name>` line anywhere in the file also keeps it (git names the last matching line, which is then the user's line or the pair). `--thu` prints the release line only.
- Release answers. Laptop `Remove-PhienNoteExclude(File, Name, Legacy)` makes no git call (it uses the scan's `excl`) and returns `removed | absent | failed`; `failed` = the file is a reparse point (or `.git/info` is one), or no path was resolved. `removed` / `absent` forget a legacy record; `failed` prints `  [<project>] lỗi: ghi chú <file>: chưa gỡ được dòng /<file> của fcode trong .git/info/exclude (liên kết, hoặc git lỗi / không trả lời kịp), lần sau thử lại`, exit 1, keeps everything. Box `unexclude(d, name, legacy, projs, releasing)` (`projs` = the config snapshot `cmd_put` passes, default `cfg_projects()`; `releasing` = the folders whose own release of this name is in the same batch) returns True when the path resolved and the line is certainly gone (file missing, line absent, or removed), False when `exclude_path` is None or `.git/info/exclude` or `.git/info` is a symlink (nothing is written through it; the same `is_link` check as `ensure_excluded`), or when a rewrite is needed and `hide_uploads` (Rule H, see the "Git stays clean" bullet) could not verify `.fcode/.gitignore` = `*\n` in `<project>` or in any other box project that shares the file (`shared_projects`: a `config.json` project value that is a string, absolute and a directory, inside a work tree, whose `git rev-parse --git-path info/exclude` is the same file, `os.path.samefile`), or git did not answer for one of the config projects it checks, or its `rev-parse` failed other than with "not a git repository" for a config project that holds a regular file `<name>` (a holder candidate, "Shared exclude files" above; for any other project such a failure skips it, the 1.3.5 rule), or `pair_holders` got no git answer about a sharing project's copy (it returns None: holding cannot be decided without that answer; nothing is written; the release waits and is retried every run, exit 1), and, right before the rewrite, `unexclude` re-reads the exclude file and recomputes the text (a line appended since the first read is kept; if nothing is left to change the release counts as done, True), and an `OSError` while reading or writing counts as not gone (the name is left out of the list); the `unexcluded` list of the reply names the True ones; it answers `kept` (reply list `noteKept`, nothing written) only when a sharing project really depends on the line (see "Shared exclude files" above). A requested name in neither `unexcluded` nor `noteKept` prints `  [<project>] lỗi: ghi chú <file>: box chưa gỡ được dòng /<file> của fcode trong .git/info/exclude (liên kết, git trên box lỗi, hoặc chưa tạo được .fcode/.gitignore), lần sau thử lại`, exit 1, nothing forgotten (the pair is still there, so the next scan sees it again). The `ghi chú <file> giờ do git theo dõi …` line of r7 is unchanged in text; for a box release it is printed with the put answer (not at planning time), not for `kept`, and not when the batch got no answer (the next run prints it). In 1.3.6 that line, and the entry in `notes.released` (the menu line `xóa được`), cover only a real removal: laptop `removed` / `absent`, box `unexcluded`. A laptop `failed` answer or a box False prints only its error line and is not listed; the record is kept, and the release line and the entry come with the run that really removes the pair. Laptop: before `Remove-PhienNoteExclude` (still no git call inside it), and only while the exclude file (the scan's `excl` path, read again at the release, after a link check: a linked `.git/info` or exclude file gives the error line) still holds fcode's line (the pair, or with `legacy` the bare line; the box asks only when `new != cur`), the run checks the other `syncRepos` folders as above: a holder prints the kept line and skips the removal, `'unknown'` prints the error line above (exit 1, everything kept), and with no line left it goes straight to `Remove-PhienNoteExclude` (`absent`).
- State file `handoff-state.json` (sha memory + legacy records). Read strictly: a missing file is empty; anything else must be a JSON object, checked by the first non-whitespace character of the raw text being `{`, then by a successful parse, then by the parsed value being an object (`42`, `null`, `[{}]`, an array of records and an empty file are all refused). A refusal stops the run before any change: `lỗi: không đọc được trạng thái ghi chú (handoff-state.json): <reason>` (`<reason>` is `không phải một đối tượng JSON` when the text does not start with `{` or the parsed value is not an object, else the parse / IO message), exit 1, until the file is repaired or deleted. Written strictly: no swallowing, a failed write throws `không ghi được trạng thái ghi chú (handoff-state.json): <reason>`, which the outer handler prints as `lỗi: …`, exit 1, the run stops there (batches already done stay). In a quick run the screen shows `phien: không đồng bộ được, xem phien.log`.
- Rule L, leftovers. fcode deletes only names that match one of its complete generated patterns, only where it put them, and only when the file is older than 1 h or (when the name carries a PID) that PID is gone. Laptop: (1) `%TEMP%\fcode-phien-<PID>-<32 hex>` and the 1.3.2 form `fcode-phien-<32 hex>` (age only), never reparse points; (2) `<name>.fcode-part-<PID>-<6 hex>` in the session dirs and the blob dir of this run's projects (recursive) and in their project roots (flat), swept after the scan; (3) `<leaf>.part-<PID>` with the leaf anchored (`exclude.part-backup.part-123` is not a match for `exclude`) beside a file fcode rewrites with `Write-PhienText`, swept by `Write-PhienText` itself right before it writes, so at the path git named; the three state files (`handoff-state.json`, `phien-status.json`, `phien-auto.json`) are also swept at the start of every real run. Box: (4) `$TMPDIR/fcode-phien-<8 of [a-z0-9_]>` owned by the user, not a symlink, age only; (5) `<name>.fcode-part-<PID>-<6 hex>` in the session and blob dirs, age only, not a symlink; (6) `exclude.fcode-part-<PID>-<6 hex>` beside `.git/info/exclude`, swept by every box write of that file (`append_exclude` for the add, `write_exclude` for the release) right before it writes, age or dead PID. (7) `.gitignore.fcode-part-<PID>-<6 hex>` in `<project>/.fcode`, swept by `write_exclude` (through `sweep_exclude_parts`) when `hide_uploads` rewrites `.gitignore`, age or dead PID, not a symlink. No guess of the exclude path, no other name, nowhere else. The 1.3.2 file `handoff-state.json.part` (no PID) is never matched.
- Strings. The v1.3.2 message `phiên lớn: <file> chưa chép xong — chạy fcode phien khi mạng tốt` is printed without backticks around `fcode phien` (as the r7 "Batches" bullet already quotes it). 1.3.6 adds one line, the `kept` line above; no other screen, log, help or menu text changes.

## Amendment A11 (2026-10-26, v1.3.2: "Thêm dự án" from the app)

Shared with the iOS worker in `add-project-contract.md` and `add-project-contract-v2.md` (the Architect's copies). Server side as built:

- `POST /api/projects` `{repo, name?}` (X-PC and auth like every mutation; a body that is not a JSON object is 400, a wrong Content-Type 415; GET is 405). `repo` is a GitHub link or `owner/repo`: `https://[www.]github.com/o/r`, `github.com/o/r`, `git@github.com:o/r.git` (host case-insensitive), then any `/`, `.git`, `?query`, `#fragment` and extra path (`/tree/main`) is dropped; any other host, `http://`, a user or port in the URL, or `owner/repo/extra` written plain is 400 `bad_repo`. The reduced text must match `^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+/[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+$` with neither part only dots (after one trailing `.git`, any case), else 400 `bad_repo`. `name` is optional (missing, null and "" all mean the lower-cased repo part); a typed one is lower-cased and loses a trailing `.git`; it must match `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]{0,63}$` and not be `home`, else 400 `bad_name` (not a string, or a control character, too). No control character anywhere (`bad_repo` / `bad_name`). The repo is judged before the name. Nothing is trimmed: a space or newline around the text is refused.
- Answer 202 `{job}` (32 hex). The job runs `fcode-add.sh <owner/repo> <name>`: `bash <dir of server.mjs>/fcode-add.sh` (install.sh copies `box/fcode-add.sh` there; a checkout runs `box/fcode-add.sh`), spawned with an argument array and no shell, stdin closed, stdout read for `R <CODE> [detail]` lines, stderr dropped, `FCODE_CFG` = this server's config.json, in its own process group. One running job per NAME: a POST for that name (any repo) while its job runs is 202 with the SAME job id and starts nothing; two POSTs at once start one run. Another name runs in parallel. A job lives in memory only: 30 min after it ends it is 404 (a running job is never dropped), and a server restart forgets all jobs (the box script itself is safe to run again).
- `GET /api/projects/jobs/<id>` -> 200 `{state: "running"|"done"|"failed", code, name, repo, via, pubkey?, keyUrl?, detail}`; unknown id 404 `no_job` (the path `/api/projects/jobs/omp-sessions` is not this route: it is the omp-sessions list of a project named `jobs`, A9). `code` null while running. `via`: `"key"` when the script printed KEY_NEW or KEY_EXISTS (the deploy-key route ended the run, also after a token run that fell back), else `"token"` when it printed TOKEN_OK, else null (running, or it stopped before choosing). `pubkey` and `keyUrl` (`https://github.com/<repo>/settings/keys/new`) only for NEED_KEY and NEED_WRITE, and only when the script's PUBKEY line is exactly `ssh-ed25519 <base64> [comment]`: anything else is dropped (a private key can never pass). `detail` is null or one clean line of at most 200 characters (control characters and escapes removed, `ghp_`-style and `github_pat_` tokens replaced by `<token>`, `//user:pass@` in a URL by `//<cred>@`), taken from the script's SSH_DETAIL, CLONE_FAIL, DIR_EXISTS, DIR_UNSAFE, HOOK_FAIL, URL_REWRITE, CRED_FAIL, CFG_CONFLICT, CFG_BROKEN or CLEANUP_FAIL line (the first one present); never for exit 0.
- Exit code -> state and code: 0 done ADDED; 30 done ADDED_WARN (detail = the CLEANUP_FAIL branch when there is one); 40 failed NEED_KEY; 41 NEED_WRITE; 42 WRITE_BLOCKED; 43 NET_FAIL; 44 REPO_ARCHIVED; 11 DIR_CONFLICT; 21 CFG_CONFLICT (but 21 with an `R ALIAS_FAIL` line, the ssh config could not be written, is FAILED); 22 CFG_BROKEN; 23 NAME_USED; 2 BAD_ARGS; 12 CLONE_FAIL; anything else, a signal or a script that cannot start FAILED. After 10 minutes the job is failed TIMEOUT at once and its whole process group gets SIGTERM; on Linux timeout(1) kills what is left 30 s later (`--kill-after`, `PC_ADD_KILL_AFTER_S`), and the server's own SIGKILL backstop comes only at +45 s (the script's TERM trap removes its clone, which can take a while). Closing the app sends SIGTERM to every running group.
- The log holds only `add-project <name> <CODE>`; the token, the private key, the config text and gh's output are never logged or returned. `PC_ADD_SCRIPT` (test-only, like PC_GH) is a command, one path or a JSON array `["cmd","arg",...]`, in place of the bash script.
- After a project is added (the script rewrites config.json by rename) the next request sees it in `/api/home`, `/api/overview` and `/api/meta`: the config reload that every route runs first now also drops the cached home project list when the `projects` object changed, so the new card shows at once (before this, up to 2 min). The home reply is built from `cfg.projectNames` in config order: each project comes from the cached list by name, a project the cache does not know yet is a `loading: true` placeholder, a removed one is gone. After such a change the next `/api/home` does not wait for the list refresh at all (the refresh runs in the background), so the new project is in the FIRST reload after the add (loading), and filled in on a later one.
- `GET /api/github/repos` (auth; GET else 405) -> 200 `{repos: [{repo, private, archived, canPush, updatedAt, onBox}]}` (`canPush` is GitHub's `permissions.push`: the user's role on the repo, a hint only. The box's token can still be refused when the project is added; the add then falls back to a deploy key) sorted by `updatedAt` descending (null last), at most 300. Source: `gh api "/user/repos?affiliation=owner,collaborator,organization_member&sort=updated&per_page=100&page=N" --jq '.[] | {...} | @json'` for N = 1, 2, 3 in turn, stopping at the first page with fewer than 100 entries (never `--paginate`: an account with thousands of repos cannot run out of time; `sort=updated` makes the first 300 the newest), one JSON object per line (a bad line is skipped; flags that are not `true` are false), 30 s timeout per page, a failing page is a failure of the whole list, the gh result cached 60 s and shared by concurrent requests (a failure is not cached). `onBox` is the config project whose `git remote get-url origin` names that repo (lower-cased owner/name, any URL form that GET /api/home accepts, the first project in config order); it is read on every request, never cached, so a project just added shows at once. No usable login (gh missing, exit 4, "gh auth login", `GH_TOKEN`, 401 or "Bad credentials") -> 200 `{repos: [], reason: "no_github_token"}`; any other gh failure -> 502 `{error: "github_unavailable"}`. gh's output is never returned.
- `box/fcode-add.sh` is the one source of the add logic (the laptop's `fcode add` calls the installed copy, see A10). Token route first: when `gh api repos/<repo> --jq .permissions.push` prints `true` (20 s limit), `FCODE_NO_TOKEN` is unset, it prints `R TOKEN_OK` and `R READ_OK`, clones `https://github.com/<repo>.git` with `-c credential.helper= -c credential.helper='!gh auth git-credential'` (the empty value resets inherited helpers), then writes the same chain into the repo's own config, an empty `credential.helper` first and the gh helper second (never global, no token in a URL or file), and runs the same hook, write check, config and verify steps as the key route. `permissions.push` is only a first filter: GitHub reports the user's role, not the token's scope (seen on the box: `push` true, then the HTTPS push got 403 "Permission to ... denied"), so the REAL write check decides: a push made by THIS run with THIS credential, never an existing ref and never a failed delete (see "A11 update r2"). If the token cannot clone (not a network error) or that write check is refused for permission (stderr "Permission to ... denied", "Write access to repository not granted", "marked as read only", `returned error: 401/403`, "Authentication failed", "could not read Username ... terminal prompts disabled"), it prints `R TOKEN_FALLBACK`, removes its own clone (a folder that was there before is never adopted: see A11 update r3), removes its temp file, releases its lock and re-runs itself with `FCODE_NO_TOKEN=1` (that run clones again): the deploy-key route (KEY_*, ALIAS_*, NEED_KEY / NEED_WRITE) then decides. Net errors (ssh and curl wording), an archived repo and a protected-branch refusal are final on the token route (43, 44, 42). Exit codes and the other `R` lines are unchanged. Tests: `test/fcode-add.test.mjs` runs the real script with a local bare repo as GitHub (git `url.<base>.insteadOf`), a fake `gh`, throwaway `FCODE_SSH_DIR` / `FCODE_WORKSPACE` / `FCODE_CFG`, plus the server running it. A project added by the token route keeps an https origin with the repo-local gh helper, so the 5-minute `fcode-git-sync` timer (which has no `GH_TOKEN` of its own) takes it from the vault file as described in A9; without it the fetch of a private repo would fail on every timer run.

### A11 update r2 (2026-10-26, review round 1 of the add-project branch)

- Write proof (box/fcode-add.sh). The check pushes ONE probe branch that only this run knows: `refs/heads/box/fcode-add-check-<name with [^a-z0-9-] as ->-<epoch>-<pid>-<random>` (suffix `[a-z0-9-]+`; the app shows this exact branch in its ADDED_WARN text), made from an empty-tree commit of this run, created with `--force-with-lease=<ref>:` (it must not exist yet) and deleted with `--force-with-lease=<ref>:<that commit>` (only its own commit). An existing branch, an "up to date" answer or a failed delete is never proof. Once the create has succeeded the write is proven; ANY refused delete (permission, archived, network, other) is only `CLEANUP_FAIL <that exact branch>` (ADDED_WARN). A TERM between the create and the delete also leaves the branch (its name is unique): accepted. Two runs on one repo under different names touch only their own probe. The old fixed `box/fcode-add-check` name is not used any more.
- Hook. Installation errors (hooks folder, file, mode, config) end the run with `R HOOK_FAIL install`, exit 24 (the server reports FAILED) before the project is registered. The clone's own `core.hooksPath` is set to its real hooks folder (repo-local), so a global or system `core.hooksPath` cannot bypass it, and the hook is verified the way git uses it: `git push --dry-run` of an empty-tree commit to `main` against a throw-away local bare repository must be refused with the hook's message, and the same to `box/x` must go through (`R HOOK_FAIL verify`, exit 24, otherwise). Running the hook file directly proves nothing and is not done. The same check gives `V_HOOK_OK` / `V_HOOK_BAD` after the project is added.
- Paths. Before anything changes, a target that is a symlink, a folder whose resolved path is not exactly `<resolved workspace>/<name>`, or whose `.git` is a symlink or whose resolved git dir is not `<folder>/.git`, is refused: `R DIR_UNSAFE unsafe`, exit 11 (DIR_CONFLICT). Any other existing folder is `R DIR_EXISTS exists`, exit 11 (A11 update r3). The workspace itself may be a symlink.
- Cleanup. The clone this run made is removed on any failure before the project is registered in config.json (hook, write check, NEED_WRITE, WRITE_BLOCKED, ARCHIVED, a failing registration) and on TERM / INT / HUP; a folder that existed before the run is never removed; after registration it is never removed. The `R` lines are written with SIGPIPE ignored, so a server that went away does not kill a running add midway. The mktemp file is removed before the TOKEN_FALLBACK re-exec (EXIT traps do not run on exec). The read-only alias-owner and key-owner checks (NAME_USED, exit 23) now run before the token route, so a fallback that would end in NAME_USED never leaves a clone.
- Durability. config.json and its `.bak-*` copy are written, flushed and fsynced before `os.replace`, and the folder is fsynced after it.
- Job lifecycle (server.mjs). On Linux the script runs under `timeout --kill-after=30 <deadline>` (`PC_ADD_KILL_AFTER_S` overrides the 30, test-only) (the same 10 minutes as the server's own timer; the code 124 maps to TIMEOUT; after --kill-after the group is killed and the server sees a signal, never a code 137), so the deadline holds when the server is gone. `main()` handles SIGTERM and SIGINT: `app.close()` (which sends SIGTERM to every running job group, and the script then cleans up and exits 143), then exit 0 (hard exit after 5 s). `KillMode=process` in install.sh is kept on purpose (tmux sessions must survive a restart); after a crash or SIGKILL the job is not killed, and ends by its own `timeout`; its output pipe is gone, which the script survives (SIGPIPE ignored); the server forgets the job (a poll answers 404 `no_job`, and a retry of the same repo and name is safe). Jobs are pruned on every submit as well as on every poll: ended ones after 30 min, and at most 50 are kept, the oldest finished first (a running job is never dropped). `PC_ADD_TIMEOUT_MS` (test-only) overrides the deadline.

### A11 update r3 (2026-10-26, review round 2: existing folders are no longer adopted)

- **A folder that already exists is never adopted; pick another name or remove it on the box.** If `<workspace>/<name>` exists in any form (directory, file, symlink, git or not), the script refuses before any change: `R DIR_EXISTS exists` (exit 11; the job code stays DIR_CONFLICT, detail `exists`), or `R DIR_UNSAFE unsafe` (exit 11, detail `unsafe`) when it is a symlink, resolves outside the workspace, or its `.git` is a link or a git dir elsewhere. The reuse path (CLONE_EXISTS, set-url on an existing clone, an inherited pushurl / insteadOf / hooksPath / credential config) is gone: every later check runs on a clone made by this run. The one exception is an already registered project: the config maps `<name>` to this folder and its `remote.origin.url` names the same repo (any URL form): the script prints `R CFG_EXISTS` and exits 0, and touches nothing (no gh call, no write check, no config or credential change). The job is then done ADDED, with `via` null.
- Credentials. Every network git call of the token route (clone, probe push) runs `git -c credential.helper= -c credential.helper='!gh auth git-credential' ...`: the empty value resets what system or global config brings, so only gh is asked and told about a credential. The clone's own config gets the same chain (an empty `credential.helper`, then the gh helper) and a failed write of it fails the add (`R CRED_FAIL config`, exit 25, FAILED; the clone is removed).
- Push destination. The probe create and delete push to the explicit URL of the chosen route (`https://github.com/<repo>.git` or the `git@github-<name>:<repo>.git` alias), never to `origin`. Before the clone (and again on the finished clone) the script refuses a git config that rewrites that URL: a `url.*.insteadOf` or `url.*.pushInsteadOf` in the system, global, repo or worktree config whose value is a prefix of it, or a `remote.origin.pushurl` (`R URL_REWRITE rewrite`, exit 26, FAILED). Settings made through `-c` or the environment of the run itself (the test harness) are not counted. Needs git 2.26 (`--show-scope`).
- Hooks. After the clone the `.git/hooks` folder, `hooks/pre-push` and `.git` must not be symlinks and must resolve inside the clone, checked before mkdir, install and chmod (else `R HOOK_FAIL install`, exit 24; the clone is removed). The repo-local `core.hooksPath` of the A11 r2 rule stays: only a GLOBAL or system `core.hooksPath` can exist now, and the box's global hooks do not run in FCode-added clones.
- Registration vs cleanup. TERM, INT and HUP are ignored for the registration step (they are not deferred: the run goes on to its end), and the Python writer reports through `os.write` and ignores a closed output. From the `os.replace` on the project is registered: a later error (the directory fsync) is a warning (`R CFG_WARN fsync`, exit 3 inside, the run ends 30), never a failure. The cleanup that removes a clone also reads config.json first: when it already maps `<name>` to this folder (and did not before the run) the folder is not removed, whatever the exit status.
- Job detail words (server.mjs ADD_DETAIL, first line with text wins): `SSH_DETAIL`, `CLONE_FAIL`, `DIR_EXISTS` (`exists`), `DIR_UNSAFE` (`unsafe`), `HOOK_FAIL` (`install` | `verify`), `URL_REWRITE` (`rewrite`), `CRED_FAIL` (`config`), `CFG_CONFLICT`, `CFG_BROKEN`, `CLEANUP_FAIL`. The app matches: DIR_CONFLICT + `exists` (or none), DIR_CONFLICT + `unsafe`, FAILED + `install` | `verify` | `rewrite` (26) | `config` (25).
- Final R codes and exit codes of box/fcode-add.sh (for the laptop owner): exit 0 done (R CFG_EXISTS alone = already registered, nothing touched); 30 done with a warning (CLEANUP_FAIL <branch>, V_*_BAD, CFG_WARN); 40 NEED_KEY (+ SSH_DETAIL, PUBKEY); 41 NEED_WRITE (+ PUBKEY); 42 WRITE_BLOCKED; 43 NET_FAIL; 44 REPO_ARCHIVED; 11 DIR_EXISTS or DIR_UNSAFE; 12 CLONE_FAIL; 2 USAGE / BAD_ARGS; 20 KEY_FAIL; 21 CFG_CONFLICT, or ALIAS_FAIL; 22 CFG_BROKEN; 23 NAME_USED; 24 HOOK_FAIL install | verify; 25 CRED_FAIL; 26 URL_REWRITE; 143 stopped by TERM/INT/HUP (clone removed); 124 only from timeout(1). Lines: KEY_NEW, KEY_EXISTS, ALIAS_ADDED, ALIAS_EXISTS, TOKEN_OK, TOKEN_FALLBACK, READ_OK, CLONED, HOOK_OK, HOOK_EXISTS, WRITE_OK, CFG_ADDED, CFG_EXISTS, V_EMPTY_REPO, V_BRANCH_OK / V_BRANCH_BAD, V_PR_OK / V_PR_BAD, V_HOOK_OK / V_HOOK_BAD, V_SERVER_OK / V_SERVER_BAD, V_CFG_BAD, RULES_YES / RULES_NO. Gone: CLONE_EXISTS, DIR_NOTGIT, DIR_OTHER.

### A11 update r4 (2026-10-26, review round 3: atomic reservation, escalation proof)

- Reservation. Right after the existence check (before the key and alias steps) the script reserves the target with ONE atomic `mkdir "$dir"` (no `-p`): if it fails the run is `DIR_EXISTS exists` (someone else made the folder in the same instant: never touched) or, when the folder is not there, `CLONE_FAIL` with mkdir's own error (exit 12, e.g. a workspace that cannot be written). From the moment mkdir succeeds the folder is owned by this run (`owned=1`): the cleanup and the token fallback remove it on every exit before the project is registered (failed or half clone, a TERM during the clone, a hook error, NAME_USED, NEED_KEY...), never after registration. TERM, INT and HUP are held across mkdir -> owned (bash runs a trapped signal only after the foreground command returns) and honoured right after (exit 143, folder removed). The mkdir itself runs in a child with TERM, INT and HUP ignored (`( trap '' TERM INT HUP; exec mkdir "$dir" )`; SIG_IGN survives exec), so a signal sent to the whole process group (timeout(1), the server's close()) cannot kill it between mkdir(2) and its result; on the failure branch a held signal ends the run (143) without touching the folder, and a dangling symlink that appeared at the target meanwhile counts as DIR_EXISTS like any other entry. The parent folder is made with a separate `mkdir -p "$ws"`.
- Rewrite before the clone. A rewrite of the https URL found before the clone (a global `url.*.insteadOf` / `pushInsteadOf` / `remote.origin.pushurl` as in A11 r3) makes the run a deploy-key run from that point: no `TOKEN_OK`, no `TOKEN_FALLBACK`, no re-exec. The key URL is checked the same way (`URL_REWRITE`, exit 26, if it is rewritten too); on the key route a rewrite is 26 at once; after the clone a rewrite is 26 on both routes.
- Lifecycle invariant. Every child of the script is waited for before the script goes on (a trapped signal runs only after the foreground command returns) or is bounded on its own: the process substitution in `url_rewrite_check` is a local `git config` read to EOF; `timeout 20 gh ...` (the permission probe and `gh pr list`) runs in its own process group with its own limit. The job's deadline is timeout(1)'s TERM then KILL to the process group, proven by the escalation tests (a TERM-ignoring job and grandchild must die within the bound; without `--kill-after` they do not); a TERM from the server's `close()` is forwarded by timeout(1), which arms the same KILL. The script must not use `&`, `nohup`, `setsid`, `disown`, `coproc` or a process substitution that is not read to EOF.
- `gh pr list` in the final verification also runs under `timeout 20` (a hang is V_PR_BAD, not a stuck job).
- Not covered (out of scope): a folder left by a hard KILL after kill-after or by a power loss in the middle of the clone (remove it on the box: `rm -rf /data/workspace/<name>`); a box hook or helper that daemonizes a TERM-ignoring process.

## Amendment A12 (2026-10-27, v1.3.3: image upload)

`POST /api/projects/<name>/upload?session=<session name>` (`session` optional). The raw image is the body; this is the only route whose body is not JSON. Server side as built:

- Auth and `X-PC` / Origin exactly like every other POST (CSRF 403 first, then 401). Other methods 405. The route is matched before the generic 64 KB JSON `readBody`, and reads its own body.
- Admission (r2): at most 2 uploads are in flight; the count is taken at route entry, before any body byte is read, and a third is answered 429 `{error:"busy"}` without reading its body (the connection is closed, see "Refused uploads"). The slot is freed on every way out (success, every error, a client that goes away). So no more than 2 upload buffers (2 x 10 MiB) exist at any time. The route runs no `git` child.
- Order of checks, each before the next costs anything: unknown project, or one whose folder is missing -> 404 `{error:"no_project"}` (the folder is never created); `Content-Type` (parameters and case ignored) not exactly `image/jpeg` or `image/png` -> 415 `bad_type`; `session` given (even empty) and not a live tmux session whose `@pc_project` is this project -> 404 `no_session` (nothing has been written by then, and `.fcode` is not created); body over 10485760 bytes -> 413 `too_big` (a declared `Content-Length` over it is refused before a byte is read; otherwise the answer comes as soon as the cap is passed, the bytes read so far are dropped and the connection is closed after the answer); empty body -> 400 `empty`; first bytes not `FF D8 FF` (jpeg) / `89 50 4E 47 0D 0A 1A 0A` (png) for the declared type -> 415 `bad_type`; a folder error while storing (also a symlinked `.fcode` or `.fcode/uploads`, which is never followed, and a `.fcode/.gitignore` that is a symlink or not a regular file) -> 500 `storage`.
- Stored as `<projectDir>/.fcode/uploads/<YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS>-<6 hex>.jpg|png` (UTC time of the server): folders created 0700 one level at a time, each checked with `lstat` (a symlink in place of either is refused), file opened `O_WRONLY|O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW` with mode 0600 (a name that exists is retried with a new random part, 5 tries). Answer 200 `{"path":"<absolute path>","attached":true|false}`. Threat model (r2): every process that can write a project folder (agents, git) runs as the same uid as the server, so a same-uid race gains no privilege; these checks stop accidents (a symlink left in the tree), not a same-uid attacker.
- Git stays clean: after the `.fcode` and `.fcode/uploads` folders are checked, and whether or not the project is in a git repository, the server makes sure `<projectDir>/.fcode/.gitignore` holds exactly the one line `*` (`*\n`), which makes git ignore everything in `.fcode`, that `.gitignore` included, in any repository above it (so also a linked work tree and a project that is a sub-folder of a repository). No `git` command is run, and nothing under `.git` (`info/exclude` included), no project `.gitignore` and no other file of the project is read or written. A correct `.gitignore` is left alone; otherwise it is written to a part file `.gitignore.fcode-part-<pid>-<6 hex>` in `.fcode` (`O_WRONLY|O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW`, mode 0600) and renamed over it (rename replaces a stale file without following a link). A `.fcode/.gitignore` that is a symlink or not a regular file is never followed or replaced: the upload is refused with 500 `storage`. `/.fcode/` lines that version 1.3.3 already put in `.git/info/exclude` stay as they are and are harmless. Crash leftover: a server killed between the part file and the rename leaves `.gitignore.fcode-part-<pid>-<6 hex>` without `.gitignore`; the server removes its own such leftovers (exact name `.gitignore.fcode-part-<digits>-<6 lowercase hex>`, regular files only, no link followed, older than 1 h) from `.fcode` only when it (re)writes `.gitignore` (a correct `.gitignore` returns early, and its `*` already ignores any leftover), and the next upload writes `.gitignore` itself. An existing `.gitignore` is read only when its size equals `*\n`. The server's writes of `.fcode/.gitignore` run one at a time inside the process (a chain shared by all projects; a failed write never blocks later ones, and each caller gets its own result), and a part file is removed only by the call that created it (a part name that already exists makes the call fail with 500 `storage` and the existing file is left alone), apart from the 1 h stale-part sweep above. Version skew (1.3.5 laptop, 1.3.3 server): a 1.3.3 server appends `/<prefix>.fcode/` to `.git/info/exclude` with `O_APPEND` on a project's first upload (and whenever that line is missing), before it creates `.fcode`. The box program of `fcode phien` adds its own pair with one `O_APPEND` write too (`append_exclude`; a write shorter than the pair is a failure and places no note), so the two appends compose and neither is lost. Its release (`unexclude`: read, part file, `os.replace`) can lose a `/.fcode/` line appended during that rewrite; so the rewrite is allowed only once the uploads folder of every folder that can receive such a line hides itself (`hide_uploads`, Rule H): the project itself and every other project of the box `config.json` that shares this `.git/info/exclude` — the same set the 1.3.3 server writes for: a value that is a string and an absolute path (`projectNames`), an existing directory (`storeUpload`), inside a work tree (`rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree`), whose `--git-path info/exclude` is this very file (`os.path.samefile`: git prints a relative path from a sub-folder and an absolute one from a linked work tree). The line it appends is `/<prefix>.fcode/`, i.e. `<worktree>/<prefix>.fcode`, the project folder's own `.fcode`, wherever the project sits in its repository. A worktree root that is not a project, another repository, a folder that is missing or not a work tree (a bare repository included) gets nothing and is skipped; git not answering for one of the config projects it checks makes the gate False (sharing cannot be decided without that answer, so the release waits). For each folder of the set it creates `.fcode` (0700) when missing (never through a link) and succeeds only when `<folder>/.fcode/.gitignore` is a regular, non-link file reading back exactly `*\n`; a missing `.gitignore`, or a regular one with other content (an empty one included), is written through `write_exclude` (part file + `os.replace`; its sweep also removes `.gitignore.fcode-part-<PID>-<6 hex>` leftovers of a dead PID or older than 1 h, Rule L (7)); a link at `.fcode` or `.gitignore`, a non-file, or an `OSError` makes it False. The rewrite is done only when the exclude text actually changes, when no sharing project depends on the line (`kept`, A10 r8 "Shared exclude files"), and only if `hide_uploads` is True for the whole set; otherwise (other than `kept`, which writes nothing and is no error; see "Shared exclude files") `unexclude` is False, nothing is written, and the release waits and is retried at every run (exit 1 with the error line above, the record kept) until `.fcode` and its `.gitignore` are real and writable in every folder of the set. No `git worktree list` is run. A lost `/.fcode/` line then exposes nothing: every file under `.fcode` is ignored by that `.gitignore`, and the 1.3.3 server re-adds its line at its next upload. Side effect: after a release in a project, `.fcode` and `.fcode/.gitignore` exist in that project and in every other box project sharing its `.git/info/exclude` (linked work trees registered as projects, sub-folder projects), even if no photo was ever sent there (the same folder and file a 1.3.4 server makes at the first upload; git does not show them). Torn append: if the box's pair is cut short and the server's `/.fcode/` lands right after it, the two patterns glue into one inert line; the note is not placed, the next run appends a fresh pair, the server's next upload re-adds its line, and the junk line stays (it ignores a path that does not exist). Recommended order: update the box server first (`git pull`, `bash install.sh`), then the laptop; a 1.3.4 server never writes `info/exclude`.
- Housekeeping: the sweep runs on upload only (nothing else triggers it): each upload, after storing, looks at the entries of that uploads folder whose name matches `^\d{8}-\d{6}-[0-9a-f]{6}\.(jpg|png)$`, `lstat`s each (a folder or a symlink is never touched, no link is followed), and deletes the regular files whose mtime is more than 7 days old. Other names are never touched. A failure on one file is ignored and the next file is still tried.
- Attach (only with `session`): the absolute path ALONE into the session's input, never Enter, as one mutation job (ordered with the other input of the server). The agent is the session's `@pc_harness`: `codex` -> one `send-keys -t =<name>: -l -- <path>` (a paste would stay text there); `claude`, `omp`, `shell`, or no agent recorded -> `load-buffer -b pc -` with the path as stdin, then `paste-buffer -p -d -b pc -t =<name>:` (bracketed paste, the same as a long `/api/send`). A path with whitespace, `'` or `"` is not attached (`attached:false`, file kept). The session is identified when the upload is accepted (name, project, agent kind, tmux creation time) and checked again inside the mutation job, right before the tmux call: if the name is gone, or now belongs to another project, another agent kind or a newer tmux session, nothing is sent (`attached:false`, file kept). `attached:true` only when tmux answered 0; a tmux failure (session gone meanwhile, queue busy) is `attached:false` with the file kept. The device is checked again once the body is in: a device revoked meanwhile gets 401 and nothing is stored. Without `session`, `attached` is false and tmux is not called. A device revoked or a client gone during the attach still ends the request as for any route.
- No change to `/api/send` or to any other route (the bracketed paste of `sendText` is now one helper, `pasteText`, which the upload shares; same tmux calls). The log line holds the path without the query (no session name).
- Timeouts (r3, replaces the r2 `readBody` timer): short by default, long only when admitted. ONE timer per request is set synchronously in the `createServer` handler, before any routing: 15 s (`bodyMs`); on expiry a request that is not complete is destroyed (a complete request, such as an SSE `GET`, is never touched). It is cleared when the request closes, not when the answer goes out, so a request that is refused with its body unread and then trickles bytes is still cut at 15 s. `readBody` has no timer of its own. Only the upload route replaces it with the long one (`uploadRequestMs`, 120 s: a 10 MiB photo on a weak link, about 0.7 Mbit/s), and only right before it reads the body, after auth, CSRF, admission (the slot), project, `Content-Type` and session have all passed. `server.requestTimeout` stays 120 s as the outer bound and `headersTimeout` is 10 s. The app still sends a downsized JPEG (longest side 2048 px, quality 0.8). Test-only `createApp` options `bodyMs` and `uploadRequestMs` shorten the two bounds.
- Client gone (r3): the upload route knows about a vanished client from its first line (`ctx.cancelled`, set by the response `close` registered before any `await`, and `req.destroyed`). After every `await` before the body is read (the project `stat`, the session list) it stops, without a response, if the client is gone; otherwise `readUpload` would wait for events of a request that has already closed and the slot would never come back. The slot is taken at admission and given back in exactly one `finally` that runs on every way out.
- Refused uploads close the connection (r3): every upload answer that is not a 200 (401, 403, 404, 405, 413, 415, 429, 400, 500) is sent with `Connection: close`, and the request is destroyed after the response `finish`. A body that was not consumed is never drained; a 413 reached in the middle of the stream drops what it has read. Known cost: a client whose body is still in flight when the socket closes gets a reset, and the reset can overtake the answer (measured on Linux and Windows loopback: a client writing megabytes sees no answer at all, only a closed connection); a client that has not gone beyond its first bytes gets the answer. Accepted: because refused uploads are closed without reading the body, an app that has already written its body usually sees a network error rather than the 429/401/404 answer, so it shows `Không gửi được ảnh, thử lại`, and a retry works.
- iOS cancel: the app lets the user cancel an image before its upload starts by tapping the `Đang gửi ảnh…` note (strings `Chạm để huỷ ảnh`, VoiceOver `Đã huỷ ảnh`); a cancelled image never reaches the server.
- Tests: `test/server.test.mjs`, tests named `upload: ...` (fake tmux, real git, throwaway project folders).
